summary: 1930s tower on the East Peak of Rattlesnake Mountain, King County WA; known from the Kresek inventory; a 1953 map shows an Airway Beacon there. Listed as gone.

facts.status_note: Register says the tower is now gone. A 1953 map shows an Airway Beacon at the East summit; no source says a lookout stands there today.

access.note: The Willhite page describes a trail to the summit with trailheads at each end. It does not say whether the summit is open to the public, or who manages it now.

visit.trail_note: A trail runs the 11-mile length of the mountain, with trailheads at each end; the page names the Rattlesnake Ledge trailhead, which it says is near North Bend off I-90.

events.note: A 1953 map shows a still-standing Airway Beacon at the East summit, at 3,517 feet (per the Willhite page)
Registered June 20, 2012 as US 1296, WA 196; nominated by Ray Kresek

evidence.supports: tower built in the 1930s and now gone
evidence.quote: Built in the 1930s, this tower is now gone.

evidence.supports: administered by Washington Division of Forestry/DNR
location about 3 miles SSW of North Bend
the Kresek lookout inventory lists a 1930s tower at the East Peak
evidence.quote: The Kresek lookout inventory lists a tower in the 1930s, giving the location and elevation of the East Peak.

evidence.supports: USGS notes of 1937 and 1956 do not mention a tower
evidence.quote: Checking the USGS notes in 1937 & 1956, they made no mention of one.

evidence.supports: 1953 map shows the Airway Beacon standing at the East summit, 3,517 feet
evidence.quote: A 1953 map (shown on right) shows the still standing Airway Beacon at the East summit, at 3,517 feet.

evidence.supports: author's reasoning that the tower would have been on Weyerhaeuser land
evidence.quote: Based on land ownership at that time, the tower would have been on Weyerhaeuser land.

evidence.supports: trail runs the length of the mountain with trailheads at each end
evidence.quote: A trail runs the entire 11 mile length of the mountain with trailheads at each end.

evidence.supports: photo caption shows an Airway Beacon at the summit (undated)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com say Rattlesnake Ridge; the Willhite page calls the site the East Peak of Rattlesnake Mountain. The 3,517 ft elevation matches on both the register and the Willhite page, so the story treats them as one site.

notes_for_editor: No source gives a build year, so no year-specific built event is recorded; the 1930s date rests on the register and firelookout.com, which take it from the Kresek inventory. The Willhite page is a personal lookouts site, and its land-ownership reasoning is the author's. Not read: the Kresek inventory itself, USGS notes, and any newspaper. The weebly Rattlesnake Ridge page was read and gives only the section and agency. Access is marked unknown: the Willhite page describes trails to the summit but does not say the summit is open to the public or who manages it now; verify both before relying on either. Retry the Kresek inventory and any 1930s newspaper item if the editor wants a build year.
